title: Pea plants explained inheritance
sources: G. H. Hardy and Wilhelm Weinberg (1908)

quiz.q: Which force does NOT disturb Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium?
quiz.why: Right. Random mating is an assumption of the equilibrium, not a force against it.

lines.say: The laws of inheritance were found in a monastery garden.

beats.say: The laws of inheritance were found in a monastery garden. With pea plants.

lines.say: Gregor Mendel published his pea experiments in 1866.
In 1908, Hardy and Weinberg described populations in genetic balance.

beats.say: Gregor Mendel published his pea experiments in 1866. In 1908, Hardy and Weinberg described populations in genetic balance.

lines.say: Segregation: each parent passes on one allele for a trait.
Independent assortment: different traits sort independently.

beats.say: Segregation: each parent passes on one allele for a trait. Independent assortment: different traits sort independently.

lines.say: Allele frequencies stay the same across generations
unless mutation, selection, migration or drift change them.
